question: Can a physically decoded internal-acceleration auxiliary reduce the observed interior H40 safety violations without erasing task motion?
physical_decode: Original Processor minmax saturation, FP64 statistics, relative SE3 EEF9 and absolute nominal grip; no extra command filter
differences: 38 interior second differences at 0.05 seconds, m/s^2; no boundary, rotation or gripper auxiliary in V1
lambda: 0.1*median(native_parameter_gradient_L2/auxiliary_parameter_gradient_L2) on 16 preregistered TRAIN windows at unchanged SFT2000; freeze before C training or DEV queries
calibration_selection: Existing fixed TRAIN40: PREGRASP 2 normal+2 recovery; DESCEND and CLOSE each 2 normal+1 recovery; LIFT and HOLD each 1 normal+2 recovery; first eligible probes within each group
lambda_zero_qualification: Two CUDA-resident noncandidate updates from the same complete A250 checkpoint; exact loss, gradients, parameters, optimizer, scheduler, RNG and native noise; then restore exact SFT2000 before calibration

evaluation.TRAIN: Existing fixed TRAIN40 x3 noises; reuse A/B saved group0
evaluation.DEV_reference: Existing fixed four reference layouts x5 phases x3 noises=60 predictions, not 60 independent scenes
evaluation.mechanism_gain: Relative to matched A: >=20 percentage points more envelope passes OR >=50% reduction in P95 acceleration excess; full denominators and phases retained
evaluation.regression_margin_basis: 20% and 40% of the original 0.05m/s *0.05s=2.5mm single-interval translation allowance; fixed before new DEV
evaluation.direction_no_collapse: For expert net displacement>=1mm, report every cosine and displacement ratio; >=90% positive cosine and median predicted/expert displacement >=0.8
